purpose: Independent practice of C1.3 — identifying the core of a repeating pattern, naming its rule using letters (AB/ABB/AAB/ABC), and extending the parade using the rule.
student_learning_goal: I can find the pattern rule and use it to keep the parade going.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can find the pattern rule and use it to keep the parade going.
header.character_watermark: Coco the Conductor in the top-right corner with a small magnifying glass — the 'crack the code' Coco. Small (~1.5in tall). References the shared 'Coco the Conductor' asset from blueprint.recurring_characters.

parts.part_title: Part 1: Match each parade to its rule
parts.student_instructions: Look at each parade. Draw a line from the parade to its rule on the right.
parts.visual_layout: Three short horizontal parade strips stacked vertically on the LEFT side of the page (each ~3.5in wide, 5–6 cells). Strip A: Bea-Finn-Bea-Finn-Bea-Finn (AB). Strip B: Bea-Finn-Finn-Bea-Finn-Finn (ABB). Strip C: Bea-Finn-Bibi-Bea-Finn (ABC). On the RIGHT side, four rule labels stacked vertically in boxes (~1in tall each): AB, ABB, AAB, ABC. Student draws lines connecting each strip to the correct rule (one rule will go unused — AAB).

parts.answer_key: Any valid 6-cell parade matching the rule the child wrote. Examples: Rule AB → Bea-Finn-Bea-Finn-Bea-Finn. Rule ABB → Bea-Finn-Finn-Bea-Finn-Finn. Rule AAB → Bea-Bea-Finn-Bea-Bea-Finn. Rule ABC → Bea-Finn-Bibi-Bea-Finn-Bibi. Correct if the parade follows the chosen rule consistently.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, draw an arrow on Part 3 pointing past the strip and write the next 4 cells your rule would create. Where would cell 10 be?
teacher_notes: Lesson 2 consolidation. Distribute at the end of the Action phase. Watch for: (a) on Part 1, children who confuse ABB with AAB — this is a common slip; encourage them to count the As and Bs in order. (b) On Part 2, children who write the rule but cannot loop the core — the loop is the visual scaffold; redirect them to draw it first. (c) On Part 3, the rule-bank prevents inventing impossible labels but does not prevent using a rule incorrectly — check that the parade actually follows the chosen rule. Use Part 2's loop and rule label as primary evidence for the Lesson 2 formative tracker columns.
